securitySettings.title: Security & Session
securitySettings.description: Configure session expiry policies and MFA device trust for all users.

sessionExpiry.title: Session Expiry
sessionExpiry.idleTimeoutHelp: Log users out after this many minutes of inactivity (max {{max}}). Set to 0 to disable.
sessionExpiry.idleDisabled: Idle timeout is disabled. Sessions will not expire due to inactivity.
sessionExpiry.maxDurationHelp: Force re-login after this many hours, regardless of activity (max {{max}}). Set to 0 for no limit. This is enforced server-side.
sessionExpiry.maxDurationDisabled: No maximum session duration. Sessions last until the user logs out.

validation.idleTimeout: Idle timeout must be between 0 and {{max}} minutes.
validation.maxDuration: Max session duration must be between 0 and {{max}} hours.
validation.mfaDuration: MFA remember duration must be between 0 and {{max}} {{unit}}.

schedulingSettings.title: Automation Minimum Interval
schedulingSettings.description: Set the minimum interval between scheduled automation runs for your organisation. This prevents automations from being scheduled too frequently. You cannot set a value lower than what your platform administrator has configured.

minInterval.label: Minimum interval (minutes)
minInterval.placeholder: Leave empty to use platform default
minInterval.helpText: The shortest interval users can select when scheduling agents. Must be at least {{floor}} minutes.

validation.belowFloor: Cannot be less than {{floor}} minutes (set by your platform administrator)

recoveryCodes.title: Recovery Codes
recoveryCodes.description: Allow users to generate backup recovery codes for MFA login. If a user loses their authenticator, they can use a recovery code to sign in.
recoveryCodes.disabledInfo: Recovery codes are disabled. Users who lose their authenticator must contact an admin for an MFA reset.

mfaSettings.title: Device Trust Duration
mfaSettings.description: Configure how long users can skip two-factor authentication on trusted devices. Set to 0 to require MFA on every login. Reducing the duration takes effect on the next login — existing device trust that exceeds the new window will require MFA again.
mfaSettings.durationHelp: Users who check 'Remember this device' will skip MFA for the selected duration (max {{maxHours}}h / {{maxDays}} days).
mfaSettings.zeroMeansAlways: MFA will be required on every login. No 'Remember this device' option will be shown to users.
mfaSettings.saveSuccess: MFA device trust settings saved successfully.

mfaReset.resetConfirmBody: This will invalidate their current authenticator and revoke all active sessions. They will have 24 hours to set up a new authenticator. Please notify the user directly — email notifications are not yet automated.
mfaReset.resetSuccess: MFA reset initiated. Grace period expires at {{expiresAt}}.
mfaReset.noMfaConfigured: This user does not have MFA configured.
mfaReset.rateLimited: Too many resets. Contact security if this is intentional.

sso.title: Single Sign-On (SSO)
sso.description: Configure SAML 2.0 single sign-on to allow users to sign in with their corporate identity provider.
sso.disabled: SSO is configured but not active.
sso.testSuccess: SSO test successful. Your identity provider is configured correctly.
sso.testFailed: SSO test failed. Please verify your identity provider configuration.
sso.enableSuccess: SSO has been enabled. Users can now sign in with their corporate credentials.
sso.disableSuccess: SSO has been disabled. Users must use username and password to sign in.
sso.deleteConfirm: Are you sure you want to remove SSO? Users will no longer be able to sign in with their corporate credentials.
sso.passwordFallback: Username and password login will remain available as a fallback for all users.

step1.title: Choose Identity Provider
step1.azureAdDescription: Microsoft Azure Active Directory or Entra ID
step1.protocolHelp: Most identity providers support SAML. Use OIDC if your IdP provides an OpenID Connect endpoint.

step2.title: Configure Your Identity Provider
step2.description: Copy these values into your identity provider's SAML configuration.
step2.metadataUrlHelp: Paste the Federation Metadata URL from your identity provider.
step2.metadataXmlPlaceholder: Paste your SAML metadata XML here...
step2.metadataXmlHelp: Alternatively, paste the raw SAML metadata XML.
step2.azureInstructions: In Azure Portal: Enterprise Applications → New Application → Create your own → Integrate any other application → Single sign-on → SAML → paste the Entity ID and ACS URL above.
step2.oktaInstructions: In Okta Admin: Applications → Create App Integration → SAML 2.0 → paste the Entity ID and ACS URL above.
step2.googleInstructions: In Google Admin: Apps → Web and mobile apps → Add App → Add custom SAML app → paste the Entity ID and ACS URL above.
step2.oidcIssuerHelp: The OpenID Connect issuer URL from your identity provider.
step2.oidcClientSecretPlaceholder: Enter client secret (leave blank to keep existing)
step2.oidcScopesHelp: Space-separated OIDC scopes. Default: openid email profile

step3.title: Attribute Mapping
step3.description: Map your identity provider's SAML attributes to Numa user fields.
step3.defaultMappingNote: Default mappings are pre-filled for your identity provider. Modify only if your IdP uses non-standard claim names.
step3.emailSourceUpn: Use UPN (User Principal Name) as email
step3.emailSourceHelp: Select UPN if your organisation's User Principal Name is the same as the user's email address. Common with Azure AD/Entra ID.

step4.title: Test & Enable
step4.description: Test your SSO configuration before enabling it for all users.
step4.testDescription: Click the button below to open a test login window. You will be redirected to your identity provider to authenticate.
step4.readyToEnable: Your SSO configuration is saved. Enable it to allow users to sign in with their corporate credentials.
step4.alreadyEnabled: SSO is currently enabled and active.

ssoOnly.title: SSO-Only Mode
ssoOnly.description: When enabled, password login is disabled. All users must sign in via SSO.
ssoOnly.enableConfirm:
Are you sure? This will disable password login for ALL users. Only SSO login will be available.

Requirements:
• At least one admin must have a native password account (for break-glass recovery)
• SSO must be tested and working

If SSO fails, use ?breakglass=1 on the login URL to access the password form.
ssoOnly.enabled: SSO-only mode enabled. Password login has been disabled.
ssoOnly.disabled: SSO-only mode disabled. Password login has been restored.
ssoOnly.activeWarning: Password login is disabled. All users must sign in via SSO. To restore password login, toggle this off.

groupMapping.title: Group Mapping
groupMapping.description: Automatically assign users to Numa groups based on their identity provider group membership.
groupMapping.claimHelp: Enter the exact SAML claim name or OIDC scope that your identity provider sends with group membership. If this value doesn't match your IdP's configuration, group mapping will have no effect.

scim.title: User Provisioning (SCIM)
scim.description: Automatically sync users from your identity provider. When enabled, adding or removing users in your IdP will create or disable them in Numa.
scim.revokeConfirm: Revoke the SCIM token? Your identity provider will no longer be able to sync users until a new token is generated.
scim.tokenWarning: Copy this token now — it cannot be retrieved again. Paste it into your identity provider's SCIM provisioning settings.
